task_description: A simulated Sawyer robot arm must move its end-effector to a target (goal) position in 3D space. In the task, the goal position is randomized between episodes, and there is no required object manipulation beyond reaching the target location.
state_description:
The observation follows a shared (constant-structure) state layout so a single policy can be used across tasks; many entries can be placeholders depending on the task. The commonly documented core layout uses the following indices: 
- obs[0:3]  XYZ coordinates of the end-effector
- obs[3]    gripper open/close scalar
- obs[4:7]  XYZ coordinates of object #1 (often unused/placeholder for Reach)
- obs[7:11] quaternion of object #1 (often unused/placeholder for Reach)
- obs[11:14] XYZ coordinates of object #2 (unused/placeholder for Reach)
- obs[14:18] quaternion of object #2 (unused/placeholder for Reach)

Note: Some env variants also include additional components such as the previous observation (frame-stacking) and an explicit goal position, yielding a larger observation vector (commonly reported as 39D). Always inspect the actual array returned by your env to confirm which fields are present. 

Action space is a 4D continuous Box(-1, 1). 
- action[0] dx: Cartesian displacement of the end-effector in x
- action[1] dy: Cartesian displacement of the end-effector in y
- action[2] dz: Cartesian displacement of the end-effector in z
- action[3] gripper control (open/close). 
For Reach, the gripper dimension is typically irrelevant and can be held constant (e.g., always closed).
goal_description: To move the end-effector to the goal position (a target point in 3D space) as accurately as possible; the goal location is randomized across episodes.
